anchor.selected_rendered_text: We train a Conv1D variational encoder with a recurrent latent-dynamics model on 195,883 unlabelled TESS two-minute light curves, freeze it, and evaluate the resulting star embedding on ten labelled tasks spanning variability classification, asteroseismology and rotation, against three baselines: the engineered features alone, an architecture-matched supervised Conv1D trained end-to-end, and an MLP on raw flux.
anchor.selected_source_text:
Self-supervised   models   promise   one   representation,   pre-trained   once   on
              unlabelled  survey  data  and  read  out  cheaply  for  many  downstream  tasks.  In
              stellar  time-domain  astronomy  that  promise  competes  with  a  strong,  cheap
              incumbent:   a   few   dozen   hand-engineered   light-curve   statistics.   We   train
              a  Conv1D  variational  encoder  with  a  recurrent  latent-dynamics  model  on
              195,883  unlabelled  TESS  two-minute  light  curves,  freeze  it,  and  evaluate
              the   resulting   star   embedding   on   ten   labelled   tasks   spanning   variability
              classification,   asteroseismology   and   rotation,   against   three   baselines:   the
              engineered    features    alone,    an    architecture-matched    supervised    Conv1D
              trained   end-to-end,   and   an   MLP   on   raw   flux.   Concatenating   the   learned
              embedding with the engineered features improves a frozen linear readout beyond
